_comment: Phrase rules a pivotal-history chapter keeps IN ADDITION to every rule in history/lint-rules.json (tools/_hw.lint_rules(project) appends these). Same shape as the base file, plus `scope`: all (default), outsideL1 (fires only outside a declared immersive passage) or insideL1 (only inside one). Patterns are compiled case-insensitive and run on the prose with quotations blanked, so a quoted speaker is never the narrator.

rules.why: the reader addressed in a sentence that carries a sourced fact. 'You' belongs to the writer's own sentences (a question, a comparison: voice.md §2a), which anchor no claim, and to a declared immersive passage; a sentence that states a fact states it in the third person

the reader placed in the past ('would have seen') outside a declared immersive passage: the modes are never silently mixed. Tell it in L0, or declare an L1 passage in `passages`. (Until v2 this rule also caught 'you'; that half is reader_address, allowed in a writer's sentence.)

a Pivotal Histories book speaks as 'we' (the writer and the reader together) and 'you' (the reader), never 'I': the series has no one person to give it to, and a reading needs its reasons more than its owner (storytelling.md §3)
an immersive passage places the reader where the sources place the soldiers; it never gives the reader, or anyone, a feeling no source records. Show what was there to see and hear

rules.pattern: \b(?:game[- ]chang(?:er|ers|ing)|revolutionary|decisive(?:ly)?|turned the tide|turn(?:ing)? of the tide|changed (?:the course of )?history|changed the world|unstoppable|invincible|(?:military|tactical|strategic) genius|ingenious|brilliant(?:ly)?)\b
rules.why: a label in place of the mechanism. Show how the edge worked, what it cost and where it stopped working (Mechanism / Cost / Limit), and let the outcome say the rest
a narrator's verdict on a people. Name them as they named themselves; a chronicler's word for an enemy stays inside a quotation, credited to the chronicler

a document as the subject of a verb of telling (history/voice.md §3). When a figure needs its author, name the PERSON who wrote it and when: 'Caesar put the relief army at …', 'the Novgorod chronicler wrote that …'
